description: A dashboard to visualize application's deployment.

targets.expr:
# Calculate average CPU usage grouped by replicaset and deployment where usage < 40%

avg by (replicaset, deployment) (
  (
    # STEP 1: Calculate CPU usage rate per container (1-minute average)
    # Filtering only containers with valid names and images from cAdvisor metrics
    label_replace(
      rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{
        metrics_path="/metrics/cadvisor",  # From cAdvisor metrics endpoint
        container!="",                     # Exclude empty container names
        image!=""                          # Exclude containers without images
      }[1m]),                              # 1-minute rate window
      
      # STEP 2: Extract replicaset name from pod name pattern
      # Pattern: pod-name-randomhash → extract "pod-name" as replicaset
      # Example: "frontend-abc123" → "frontend"
      "replicaset", "$1", "pod", "(.+)-[a-z0-9]+$"
    )
  )
  * 
  # STEP 3: Join with pod labels to get application group
  # Add rems_application_group label from pod labels
  on(pod) group_left(rems_application_group)
  kube_pod_labels{
    rems_application_group="$ApplicationGroup",  # Filter by selected app group
  }
) < 0.40  # STEP 4: Filter for CPU usage less than 40%

panels.description: CPU usage greater than 40% and  less than 75%
panels.title: Ideal Usage

targets.expr:
# Alert: Detects deployments with memory usage below 40% of their limit
# Purpose: Identify underutilized workloads where memory limits could be optimized

avg by (replicaset, deployment) (
  (
    # Calculate memory utilization percentage per container
    # Formula: (Actual memory usage / Memory limit) * 100
    (
      # STEP 1: Get actual memory usage (in bytes)
      label_replace(
        container_memory_usage_bytes{
          metrics_path="/metrics/cadvisor",  # Source: cAdvisor container metrics
          container!="",  # Exclude system/empty containers
          image!="",      # Exclude init containers
        },
        # Extract replicaset name from pod naming pattern
        # Example: "app-deployment-abc123" → "app-deployment"
        "replicaset", "$1", "pod", "(.+)-[a-z0-9]+$"
      )
      /
      # STEP 2: Get configured memory limit (in bytes)
      label_replace(
        container_spec_memory_limit_bytes{
          metrics_path="/metrics/cadvisor",
          container!="",
          image!="",
          # Note: Excludes containers without memory limits (returns no data)
        },
        "replicaset", "$1", "pod", "(.+)-[a-z0-9]+$"
      )
    ) * 100  # Convert ratio to percentage (0-100%)
  )
  *
  # STEP 3: Enrich with application group label for filtering
  on(pod) group_left(rems_application_group)
  kube_pod_labels{
    rems_application_group="$ApplicationGroup"  # Filter by selected app group
  }
) < 40  # Threshold: Memory usage less than 40% of limit

# Result: Shows deployments using less than 40% of their allocated memory
# Useful for: Right-sizing requests/limits, cost optimization, resource efficiency

panels.description: memory usage greater than 40% and less than 75%
panels.title: Ideal Usage

targets.expr:
# Alert: Detects deployments with memory usage exceeding 75% of their limit
# Purpose: Identify workloads at risk of OOM (Out-Of-Memory) kills

avg by (replicaset, deployment) (
  (
    # Calculate memory utilization as percentage of limit
    # Formula: (Actual memory usage ÷ Memory limit) × 100
    (
      # STEP 1: Get current memory usage (working set) in bytes
      label_replace(
        container_memory_usage_bytes{
          metrics_path="/metrics/cadvisor",  # Source: cAdvisor container metrics
          container!="",  # Filter out empty container names (system containers)
          image!="",      # Filter out init containers and sidecars
        },
        # Extract replicaset name from pod naming convention
        # Pattern: <deployment-name>-<random-suffix> → <deployment-name>
        # Example: "redis-7cbb49cd8" → replicaset="redis"
        "replicaset", "$1", "pod", "(.+)-[a-z0-9]+$"
      )
      /
      # STEP 2: Get configured memory limit in bytes
      label_replace(
        container_spec_memory_limit_bytes{
          metrics_path="/metrics/cadvisor",
          container!="",
          image!="",
          # Note: Returns no data for containers without memory limits
        },
        "replicaset", "$1", "pod", "(.+)-[a-z0-9]+$"
      )
    ) * 100  # Convert ratio to percentage (0-100%)
  )
  *
  # STEP 3: Enrich with application metadata for filtering
  on(pod) group_left(rems_application_group)
  kube_pod_labels{
    rems_application_group="$ApplicationGroup"  # Filter by selected application
  }
) > 75  # Threshold: Memory usage exceeds 75% of limit

# Result: Shows deployments using more than 75% of allocated memory
# Critical for: Preventing OOM kills, capacity alerts, urgent scaling decisions
# Action items: Increase memory limits, scale horizontally, optimize application memory

targets.expr:
# Alert: Detects services with perfect 100% success rate
# Purpose: Identify services with no HTTP errors (all requests successful)

(
  # Calculate success rate percentage for each service
  sum by (service_name) (
    # Count of successful HTTP requests
    # Includes: 2xx (Success) and 3xx (Redirection) status codes
    traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_count{
      span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",  # Filter: Only server-side spans
      http_status_code=~"^2.*|^3.*"  # Regex: Codes starting with '2' or '3'
      # Examples: 200, 201, 301, 302, 304
    }
  )
  /
  # Total count of all HTTP requests (regardless of status code)
  sum by (service_name) (
    traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_count{
      span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER"  # Same filter for denominator
      # Includes: 2xx, 3xx, 4xx (client errors), 5xx (server errors)
    }
  )
) * 100 == 100  # Condition: Exactly 100% success rate

# HOW IT WORKS:
# 1. For each service, count successful requests (2xx/3xx)
# 2. For each service, count total requests (all status codes)
# 3. Divide successful by total to get success ratio (0.0 to 1.0)
# 4. Multiply by 100 to convert to percentage (0% to 100%)
# 5. Filter for services where percentage equals exactly 100%

panels.title: 100% Success Rate

targets.expr:
# Alert: Services with very high traffic (6001-60000 requests/sec)
# Purpose: Identify heavily loaded services that may need attention

# PART 1: Services receiving MORE than 6000 requests per second
sum by(service_name) (
  rate(
    traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_count{
      service_name=~".*",           # Include all services
      span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER"  # Only count server-side requests
    }[1m]  # Average over 1 minute
  )
) > 6000  # Must exceed 6000 RPS
and
# PART 2: Services receiving 60000 or FEWER requests per second
sum by(service_name) (
  rate(
    traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_count{
      service_name=~".*",
      span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER"
    }[1m]
  )
) <= 60000  # Up to 60000 RPS

# TRAFFIC SCALE EXPLAINED:
# 6001-60000 RPS = 6K-60K requests per second
# That's:
# - 360K-3.6M requests per minute
# - 21.6M-216M requests per hour
# - 518M-5.1B requests per day

panels.title: Active

targets.expr:
# Alert: Count active alerts by category for selected application group
# Purpose: Provides a summary view of ongoing issues across the application

count by (alertname, namespace, severity, pod) (
  # Source: All active alerts from the "Servicehealth.rules" alert group
  ALERTS{
    alertgroup="Servicehealth.rules",  # Filter alerts from specific rule group
    rems_application_group="$ApplicationGroup"  # Filter by selected app group
  }
)

# HOW THIS WORKS:
# 1. ALERTS{}: Prometheus metric containing all firing alerts
# 2. Filter: Only alerts from "Servicehealth.rules" alert group
# 3. Filter: Only alerts for the selected application group
# 4. count by(): Group and count alerts by these dimensions

title: Summary
